FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–4 YEARS

Opposite Flashcards for Preschoolers

Twelve cards in six honest opposite pairs: a big ball beside a small ball, a tall tree beside a short one, a full glass beside an empty one. Show each pair side by side, say both words together, then go find the opposites hiding in your house.

These cards belong to Preschool · Age 3 on the Kiddo School learning path.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Always show the pair together

    Opposites are comparison words, so a single card teaches only half the idea. Show the big ball and the small ball side by side, say both words in one breath — “big ball, small ball” — and let your child point to each as you go.

  2. 02

    Start with the pair your child already feels

    Full and empty happens at every snack, and open and closed happens at every door. Begin there — a word attached to something your child did five minutes ago sticks far better than a new word on a screen.

  3. 03

    Let your child be the quiz master

    Once two pairs feel easy, hand the cards over: your child shows a card and asks YOU for the opposite. Getting one wrong on purpose — “the opposite of hot is… a tree?” — keeps the game alive for weeks.

  4. 04

    Put today’s pair somewhere useful

    Tape the full and empty cards by the snack cupboard, or open and closed by the door. Every trip past them is one more quiet repetition, and repetitions — not sessions — are what make comparing words stick.

      FLASHCARD · OPPOSITES & COMPARING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Big ball Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The big ball fills its whole card — and “big” only means something next to something small, which is why this card is always shown beside the small ball. Big is one of the first comparing words children truly own, because they live it all day: big spoons, big boxes, big hugs.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Starts comparing with the biggest thing in the toy basket — a ball worth hugging.

      Act both sides

      Stomp like a giant, then creep tiny like a mouse — both sides of big.

      What it teaches

      That big is a comparison — big next to what, exactly?

      Print it like this

      Print both ball cards together — the pair does the teaching.

      Grown-up tip

      Ask which things are bigger than the dog and enjoy the answers.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · OPPOSITES & COMPARING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Small ball Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The small ball is the little half of the pair — same round shape, same ball-ness, a completely different size. “Small” lands best right after “big”, when the two cards sit side by side and the difference is impossible to miss.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Gives the little one its due — small things are the best hiders in the house.

      Act both sides

      Act both sides: bear-hug arms for big, fingertip pinch for small.

      What it teaches

      Precision grip work — small fingers get stronger with small things.

      Print it like this

      Small print on purpose — a small ball card should stay humble.

      Grown-up tip

      Small balls roll under radiators; check there before anywhere else.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · OPPOSITES & COMPARING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Tall tree Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The tall tree reaches right to the top of its card, the way tall things reach past everything around them. Tall is a comparing word children meet with their whole body: they stand up tall, they stretch up tall, and they line up against the door frame to find out just how tall they are.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Covers lamp posts, doors and every tree your chin has to point at.

      Act both sides

      Grow like a beanstalk, then shrink to a toadstool; hold each pose five counts.

      What it teaches

      Height vocabulary that starts with the whole body looking upward.

      Print it like this

      Laminate this one; outdoor hunts are its natural habitat.

      Grown-up tip

      The park has more trees than the garden; take the card walking.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · OPPOSITES & COMPARING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Short tree Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The short tree stands low and friendly, about the height a tree would be if it came up to your child’s chin. Beside the tall tree the comparison is instant — and “short” becomes a word children happily use on themselves, on pets, on the step stool.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Gives short its moment: the little tree is the one at climbing height.

      Act both sides

      Crouch-walk like a short tree, then spring up tall; alternate on your call.

      What it teaches

      Comparing heights: taller than a chair, shorter than the table.

      Print it like this

      Half-size print feels right; short trees keep things modest.

      Grown-up tip

      Measure a child against a doorframe and mark it; growth is personal.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · OPPOSITES & COMPARING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Long pencil Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The long pencil stretches across its whole card from tip to end — the clearest “long” a three-year-old ever meets, because pencils are already the most important long things in a preschooler’s life. Beside the short pencil, the comparing is easy to see and easy to say.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Hands long a champion — one pencil stretching across the whole drawing.

      Act both sides

      Stride huge steps out, then return in the tiniest steps you own.

      What it teaches

      Length as a comparison — and the reach a good drawing needs.

      Print it like this

      Print it and park a real pencil alongside for honest comparing.

      Grown-up tip

      Compare shoelaces, then scarves, then corridor length; escalate sensibly.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · OPPOSITES & COMPARING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Short pencil Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The short pencil is the well-loved stub every household owns — sharpened down to a friendly little fellow with many drawings behind it. It is “short” in the most honest way: it used to be long, and holding the two cards together tells that whole story without a single extra word.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Defends the tiny pencil that still writes perfectly well, thank you.

      Act both sides

      Draw a long snake, then a short worm; pin both up for judging.

      What it teaches

      Measuring by eye — spotting short at a glance, no ruler needed.

      Print it like this

      Two copies, and cut one shorter — an instant matching puzzle.

      Grown-up tip

      Sharpen a stub and watch it graduate; every pencil was short once.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · OPPOSITES & COMPARING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Full glass Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The full glass is filled right to the top — a picture your child knows from every mealtime. Full is one of the easiest opposites to act out, because cups fill and empty all day long: water at the sink, milk at the table, bathwater everywhere.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Covers the proudest word at the table — a cup filled to the brim.

      Act both sides

      Carry the heavy full bag like a porter, then the empty one like a feather.

      What it teaches

      Quantity words from daily life — full, and soon its partner.

      Print it like this

      Kitchen wall, eye level; meal times are where this word lives.

      Grown-up tip

      Ask for more or call it full; both answers count as vocabulary.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · OPPOSITES & COMPARING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Empty glass Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The empty glass has given everything away — and children adore this word, because “all gone!” is already one of their favourite announcements. This card gives that everyday exclamation its proper name: not just gone, but empty.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Names the cup with nothing left — and the triumphant shout that follows.

      Act both sides

      Run the tap: fill for full, drain for empty, cheer for both.

      What it teaches

      Understanding "none" — empty is the number zero wearing a cup.

      Print it like this

      Splash zone placement: by the sink or taped to the high chair.

      Grown-up tip

      Hand over the judging: is this cup full, empty, or sneaky-half?

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Hot soup Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The hot soup steams right off the card — the warmest picture in the set. Hot is a word children learn carefully, because grown-ups say it in a serious voice: hot soup, hot tea, hot stove. This card lets them own the word safely, from a comfortable distance.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Teaches the most useful caution word in the kitchen, steam included.

      Act both sides

      Flap hands at the hot pan, then wrap arms, shiver, chatter like it is January.

      What it teaches

      Caution plus curiosity: hot things are interesting, from a sensible distance.

      Print it like this

      Steam is the story here — print in colour if you can.

      Grown-up tip

      Warm is for wrists, hot is for watching; keep that line bright.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · OPPOSITES & COMPARING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Cold ice cream Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The cold ice cream is the chilliest card in the set — a scoop that has to be eaten quickly before the opposite of cold happens. Children meet cold with their whole body: cold spoons, cold milk, cold hands from the freezer, and this very urgent dessert.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Cools the set down with the tastiest word in the pair.

      Act both sides

      Waddle like a penguin carrying cold shopping, then thaw dramatically on the sofa.

      What it teaches

      Feelings made into words — temperature talk starts with the fun half.

      Print it like this

      This one earns its keep by June — print it for summer.

      Grown-up tip

      Radiator, then window glass: a two-stop tour of the day's temperature.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · OPPOSITES & COMPARING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Open door Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The open door stands wide, inviting — the picture of “come in”. Open is a doing word as much as a comparing word: children open doors, boxes, books and lids all day long, so this card names something their hands already know by heart.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Names the busiest verb in the house — doors, cupboards, books, biscuit tins.

      Act both sides

      Drawbridge duty: arms up for open, arms down for closed, ships pass beneath.

      What it teaches

      Verbs in the wild: open does things, not just describes them.

      Print it like this

      One sheet, both door cards, folded down the middle like a hinge.

      Grown-up tip

      Real doors beat card doors; start with the garden gate.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · OPPOSITES & COMPARING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Closed door Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The closed door is shut tight — the other half of the pair, and a word your child meets a dozen times a day at home. Beside the open door the comparison tells the whole story: one stands wide, one is shut, and both words name what the door is doing right now.

      Teaching tips

      What this pair teaches

      Explains the gentle art of shut — for naps, for siblings, for very important meetings.

      Act both sides

      Both sides now: fling wide for arrivals, click shut for bedtime; encore optional.

      What it teaches

      That closed can be cosy: a shut door means rest, not missing out.

      Print it like this

      Stick it low on an actual door for effortless real-life matching.

      Grown-up tip

      Practise whispers behind closed doors; quiet doors make excellent dens.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Opposites & Comparing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.
